data.narrative:
Phantom Space is a Growth-stage space and aerospace company founded by Jim Cantrell, Michael D'Angelo, and Michal Prywata. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, Planet Labs, Impulse Space, and Apex Space, for a total comp set of 13 companies.

Standard triangulation methods encountered material constraints. Peer-median analysis was not applicable: while 11 same-sector peers exist in Space & Aerospace, zero same-stage, zero adjacent-stage, and zero similar-tier datapoints met the minimum threshold of 3 comparables required for reliable median derivation. Public-comp anchoring using the sector P/S median of 23.9x across the 6 public tickers could not proceed due to the absence of disclosed revenue figures for Phantom Space—a typical limitation in private company analysis.

The lack of applicable quantitative methods means a valuation range cannot be supported by this data alone. Key uncertainties preventing triangulation include: (1) absence of revenue or financial metrics for the target, (2) insufficient clustering of Phantom Space among peers by stage or scale, and (3) reliance on private peer valuations, which typically remain undisclosed. A completed valuation would require either disclosure of target revenue alongside the 23.9x public sector multiple, or identification of at least 3 sufficiently comparable private transactions at similar stage and scale.
